summary: Proceed as a rewrite stage with no companion runs. Two CTAs per SM at 80 registers is physically reachable for the low class, because at T=753 the consumer never needs master's 232-register NB=128 budget. V32 should fit 104 consumer registers with room to spare and V64 is tight but plausible. Fix the producer/consumer register split (use 32/104, not 24/104), and expect V32 to fail the skewed-routing gate because of chunk splitting.
justification: MECHANISM. Profile job 07a069bc: the low class runs rega_kernel<true,false> at 282.4/257.8 us and <false,false> at 146.0/125.2 us, about 2.1 TB/s on ~906 MB against a ~189 us byte floor, so there is about 2x headroom. Bytes in flight are ruled out twice: the moe deep ring went from STAGES 4 to 7/10 with flat 1.83->1.87 TB/s, and today's LESSONS line agrees. That leaves issue and latency in the consumer. Back-of-envelope per 9216 B stage per SM: the 8 consumer warps issue about 180 dequant instructions each, about 1440 warp-instructions, or about 360 clk over 4 schedulers. The wgmma m64n32k16 x8 per warpgroup costs about 128 clk of tensor time, about 256 clk for both WGs. The byte budget at 4.8 TB/s is about 440 clk per stage, and the measured time is about 1000 clk. The kernel therefore sits at roughly 2-3x its issue floor, with a serial dequant -> commit -> wait<0> -> arrive chain per WG and only 2 consumer warps per scheduler. That is the latency-bound picture TLP is meant to fix. The ceiling after doubling warps is the dequant ALU issue (~360 clk/stage, ~4.5 TB/s at best), so ~3 TB/s is a reasonable target. Variant B (double-buffered A) being no faster is the strongest counter-evidence, because it is the ILP version of the same latency hiding. But ptxas commonly serializes register-A wgmma when fragment registers are rewritten near in-flight groups, so B's null does not transfer to TLP. REGISTERS (the asked-for hard look). master's 232 is sized for the NB=128 bucket: acc 64 + a0[8][4] 32 + ~30-40 addressing/item/loop. At T=753 a soft routing gives about 24-45 local routes per expert, so master already runs mostly the NB=32/64 buckets and never needs 232. Consumer live set at peak, inside the 8-mma issue: V32 (max bucket 32) has acc 16 + a0 32 + about 25-35 (Item m 6, smem/ep/full0/empty0/n/kb/s/slab/KS/cw/lane/ctid, gs/sorted_ids/out pointers, err/dead) = about 75-85 <= 104, so it should be spill-free. V64 (max bucket 64) has acc 32 + a0 32 + the same = about 90-100 at peak, plus transient dq_stage temporaries (uint4 q, uint2 sc, hs[4], fs). That is tight against 104 and could spill a few words. ptxas allocates one budget for the whole switch region, so the NB=64 case decides it. The localSizeBytes==0 gate catches this and turns V64 OFF without hanging; my estimate is about 60-70% that V64 compiles clean. The producer side is the real defect in the spec. Master gives it 40 registers. 24 is spill-prone for decode_item (two integer divisions, five table loads), the 64-bit wsrc arithmetic, the expect_tx/bulk_g2s/tma_2d sequence and the mbar_wait timeout state. Use dec 32 / inc 104 instead: 32x128 + 104x256 = 30720 = exactly 384x80, which is legal because dec frees 6144 and inc takes 6144. The fallback is 40/96 (29696) only if V64 at 104 still spills, which is unlikely since 96 is worse for V64. SMEM checks out: V64 w2 95232 + ~14.3 KB static = ~109.6 KB, x2 + 2 KB reserve = ~221 KB <= 228 KB. V32 has ample room. Remember that the slab TMA boxes are already per bucket (16<<bucket rows), so NMAX only bounds which buckets exist and the stage/epilogue reservation. Shrink SLAB_HALF to NMAX rows per stage, with each half still 1024-aligned. EXPECTED: turn_1 faster, turn_4/first_turn unchanged is consistent with a low-class-only gate. Saving ~100-140 us of 428/383 us is ~13-18% of sliding turn_1, a ~3% headline move at most, which is inside LESSONS' 7-10% turn_1 drift. Judge it on the rega_kernel<G,false,64|32,...> rows, not the headline. WEAKEST LINK: chunk splitting under the narrower slab. Each extra chunk re-dequantizes the full weight tile, and dequant ALU is exactly the resource being saturated. At the judge's soft routing (~1.8x random local routes per FINDINGS, i.e. ~40-45 per expert at T=753), V32 splits most experts. Dequant work grows ~1.5-2x, so V32 will likely lose the skewed half of the worse-of-two gate. V64 splits only the popular experts. The whole result therefore rests on V64 compiling without spills. Second-weakest: ptxas may report numRegs < 80 if it does not need 80. The pool would then be short of 30720 and setmaxnreg.inc would hang. The spec's numRegs==80 requirement makes that a clean OFF rather than a hang, but it could switch both candidates OFF for a benign reason.
confounders: experts-turn-rega-s4-first-turn-n128 (parent, landed): the template refactor (NMAX/STG/OCC parameters, setmaxnreg immediates via template constants, SLAB/EPI sized by NMAX) touches the kernel source shared by the 'high' and 'ft' instantiations. If <G,BIG,128,4,1> does not produce identical SASS, turn_4/first_turn drift becomes attributable to the refactor, not noise. The build is a new extension (v3), so print numRegs/localSizeBytes/smem for the master instantiations and assert they equal v2's, which is the cheapest stand-in for byte identity.

experts-turn-rega-s4-port-t4096 (landed): it is the low-class incumbent the gate compares against. No interaction beyond being the baseline. Its single-CTA tail at 132 CTAs is replaced by a 264-CTA stride, so any change in tail/wave quantization is part of the change, not a confounder.

stack-tonight-five-prefill (landed): its _align_parallel produces the block table the kernel cuts into chunks (CH = NMAX/16). Narrower chunks depend on the align keeping each expert's blocks contiguous (error word 4). This holds today and needs no A/B. The queued align-two-phase-all-t-rega is independent but must keep that invariant if both land.
interference: No companion runs. This is a rewrite stage with an in-prepare interleaved gate against master's own low class, per-candidate printed TB/s, and distinct template names in the profile, so the single check already attributes the result. A gain shows as rega_kernel<G,false,64|32,...> rows on turn_1 below 282/146 us. A null is readable from the printed per-candidate TB/s (latency hiding did not help, so the limiter is per-item/producer/ALU issue). The one ambiguity a companion could resolve is whether a gain comes from 2 CTAs/SM or from the narrower slab and shallower ring alone. That costs nothing to settle inside prepare: also build a print-only, never-selectable diagnostic V64 at OCC=1 (<G,false,64,3,1>, master's 40/232 split) and print its gate median next to V64-OCC2. Because bytes in flight are already ruled out, the OCC1-vs-OCC2 gap isolates TLP. With 2 prefill checks left today, spending one on a companion would be waste.
rules_flags: None blocking. Dispatch on T and a prepare-set int is allowed. The variant must live in the state dict (as specified), not a module global, so both judge states carry it.
Gate routings (random and synthetic skewed) are prepare-time inputs only. The choice must stay shape-based in kernel_fn, with no per-call routing-dependent dispatch.

Never launch a candidate whose numRegs/localSizeBytes/occupancy check failed. An unchecked setmaxnreg.inc on a short pool hangs the judge, and a timeout costs the check. Run the attribute check before any eager self-check launch, not only before the gate.

Prepare time: four extra instantiations (2 G x 2 V, plus the optional diagnostic) add perhaps 30-50 s of nvcc time to a ~115-130 s prepare. Keep the existing ft deadline (150 s) and copy deadline (255 s) authoritative and skip the new candidates first, as the spec says.
open_questions: Does ptxas emit numRegs exactly 80 for __launch_bounds__(384,2) with setmaxnreg present, or could it choose less? If less, the 32/104 split no longer fits and the candidate goes OFF. Print it, and consider an alternate immediate set keyed off the reported value (e.g. 24/96 for 72) as a second compiled variant only if this happens.

Does V64's consumer region fit 104 registers at the NB=64 bucket without local memory? If V64 spills, a V64 with the NB=64 case dropped is just V32. A better fallback is dequantizing one 64-k record at a time (a0[4][4], 16 registers, two commit/wait pairs per stage), which frees 16 registers per consumer at the cost of one more wait per stage.

Actual local-route distribution at the judged turn_1 shape: mean and max routes per local expert at T=753 soft routing. This decides how often V32/V64 split chunks. Print the max chunks per expert in the gate line for both routings.
Does 264-CTA striding change the tail? w13/w2 item counts at T=753 divided by 132 vs 264 CTAs. Print items per CTA.

Keep the per-candidate w13 and w2 kernel-graph us separate: the w2 kernel (K = intermediate, fewer items) may respond differently from w13 and could justify a mixed pick (e.g. V64 for w13, master for w2).
